claims.statement: Content fields are sealed into `enc.v1.<nonce-b64url>.<ct-b64url>` envelopes with AES-256-GCM, a fresh 96-bit random nonce per encryption, AAD binding each envelope to its context.
Wrapped DEKs use `kw.v1.<nonce-b64url>.<ct-b64url>`; the KEK is HKDF-SHA256(masterKey, salt='', info='life/dek-wrap/v1') and is used only for DEK wrapping, never for content.
Master-key rotation rewraps the DEK (`rewrapDek`) and preserves the DEK bytes, so content ciphertexts are untouched and no re-encryption of stored rows is needed.
Master keys are 32-byte base64 values loaded fail-closed from per-service `<SERVICE>_MASTER_KEY` env vars at boot; errors name the variable and never contain key material.

One `user_keys` row per owner stores the `kw.v1` wrapped DEK; writes provision lazily on first content write, reads never provision and fail closed on a missing row, and the plaintext DEK lives only in a process-local memo that is never serialized or logged.
Each service derives DEKs from its own master key, so two services' stores never share a KEK even though they share the `user_keys` table shape.

The cache is inside the at-rest boundary: it stores serialized rows as persisted (ciphertext for content) and refuses values without an `enc.v1.` envelope on write-back, so plaintext can never land in Redis.
The envelope implementation is pinned to published NIST CAVP AES-GCM known-answer vectors (gcmEncryptExtIV256.rsp) compared byte-for-byte.
Any authentication failure (tamper, wrong key, AAD mismatch) surfaces as CryptoError; the open path never returns partial plaintext and no fallback plaintext exists anywhere in the design.
